behaviour_covered: two spaced filenames on one message each keep their own comment line and line number at width=1
three locations, mixed enclosed and plain filenames, all rendered intact at width=1
byte-exact comment text for an enclosed filename and line number the benchmark does not use
locations stay intact and per-location at a comfortable width (regression guard)
the wrapping primitive never splits an enclosed filename, so isolate markers stay balanced per line
why_not_duplicate: The benchmark test patch asserts exactly one enclosed location at width=1 with an integer line number, i.e. a single point. These tests add: the multi-location path (2 and 3 locations, mixed enclosed/plain), a different filename and line number for an exact-text assertion, the roomy-width regression guard, and a direct assertion on babel.util.TextWrapper -- the primitive the fix actually changed. None of these assertions is present in the benchmark test.
authoring_notes: Assertions were validated against the real behaviour of BOTH revisions before admission.

This filter removed an assertion I first expected to discriminate: at width=24 the PO layer behaves identically before and after the fix, so a test written at that width would have passed while measuring nothing.

It also surfaced a genuine limit of the fix: at narrow widths a long enclosed filename is still split by _handle_long_word, so no assertion here claims otherwise. Recording that limit is more useful than excluding the task.
One assertion initially failed on the gold patch because I omitted the '#: ' comment prefix; only executing the test revealed it.
